title: Sustainable and synthetic carbon polymers for safe and efficient H2 storage
material_description: CS-835-52 | N-containing carbon microspheres: phloroglucinol/glyoxylic acid polymer microspheres crosslinked with triethylenediamine (microwave-assisted sol-gel, 50 °C, 2.5 h), carbonized at 850 °C under N2, then CO2-activated at 835 °C for 24 h (burn-off 52 wt%)
activation_method: CO2 physical activation at 835 °C for 24 h in a vertical tube furnace (235 mL/min CO2; 0.52 g bed); burn-off 52 wt%, BO/t 2.17 wt%/h
source_location: main p.6, Fig. 3a, series CS-835-52 (green squares)
notes: archive: HYC-0076_fig3a_CS-835-52.json. Other markers of this isotherm not extracted: the 11 markers below ~5 bar are hidden behind the CS-845-64/CS-855-65/CS-865-66 markers and were not separable. Hiden XEMIS gravimetric analyser; degassed in situ at 200 °C (10 °C/min) for 4 h; sample mass "at least 50 mg" loaded (dry weight >20 mg), not stated exactly; H2 BIP+ (Air Products), purity not given as a number; base vacuum <1e-6 mbar (instrument, not stated as degas end pressure). Characterization (Table 3): A_BET 1938 m2/g (N2 at -196 °C, Micromeritics ASAP 2020, BET via BETSI software; P/P0 range and consistency criteria not stated); Vp 0.81 cm3/g = single-point total pore volume at p/p0 0.95 (N2); Vmicro (<2 nm) 0.76, V<1nm 0.47 (stored as ultramicropore volume, cutoff 1 nm), V<50nm 0.78 cm3/g from 2D-NLDFT heterogeneous-surface kernel dual fit to N2 and H2 (-196 °C, 1 bar) isotherms (SAIEUS). Composition (Table S1, elemental analysis): N 2.96 wt%, O 2.82 wt%. Class doped_carbon: N (~3 wt%) from the triethylenediamine crosslinker is built into the carbon and discussed as N-doping retained after CO2 activation.
basis_evidence: All isotherms and reported uptake data in this work are in terms of total adsorption. This must be derived from the measured, net isotherm by accounting for the skeletal density and pore volume of the adsorbent [23]. Net uptake isotherms were converted to excess uptake isotherms using skeletal (He) densities as measured on a Micromeritics Accupyc II. [...] Conversion from excess to total uptake isotherm was then performed using the single point total pore volume determined in Section 2.2. (main p.3, Section 2.3)
free_volume_calibration: buoyancy (net-to-excess) correction using skeletal He density measured on Micromeritics AccuPyc II at room temperature
